title: Polynomial growth of a positive lattice monoid length convolution
statement:
Let $r,d\ge0$ be integers, let $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ be a free abelian group (a free $\mathbf Z$-module with finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), and let $P\subseteq G$ be a finitely generated additive submonoid whose generated subgroup is $G$. Assume there is a homomorphism $w:G\to\mathbf Z$ strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Define $\nu(0)=0$ and, for $p\ne0$, let $\nu(p)$ be the largest length of a decomposition of $p$ into nonzero elements of $P$. These integers are finite, and $S_n=\{p\in P:\nu(p)<n\}$ is finite for every $n\ge1$. Let $\lambda:\mathbf Z_{\ge1}\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ be nondecreasing, and suppose there are constants $a,b>0$ and $k_0\ge1$ such that $a k^d\le\lambda(k)\le b k^d$ for every integer $k\ge k_0$. Set
$$F(n)=\sum_{p\in S_n}\lambda(n-\nu(p))\qquad(n\ge1).$$
There exist constants $a',b'>0$ and $n_0\ge1$ such that
$$a'n^{d+r}\le F(n)\le b'n^{d+r}\qquad(n\ge n_0).$$
More precisely, when $r>0$, choose nonzero monoid generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ and put $M=\max_i w(g_i)$. Then $w(p)/M\le\nu(p)\le w(p)$ for every $p\in P$. In any fixed lattice coordinates, if the integer $C\ge1$ bounds all $|(g_i)_j|$, then $|S_n|\le(2Cn+1)^r$. There exist $r$ linearly independent generators $v_1,\ldots,v_r$; for any such choice put $W=\max_j w(v_j)$. For every integer $n\ge2$, the map
$$\{0,\ldots,\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor\}^r\longrightarrow P,\quad (b_j)\longmapsto\sum_jb_jv_j$$
is injective with image contained in $\{p:\nu(p)\le n/4\}$. In particular
$$(\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor+1)^r\lambda(\lfloor n/2\rfloor)\le F(n)\le(2Cn+1)^r\lambda(n).$$
When $r=0$, one has $P=\{0\}$ and $F(n)=\lambda(n)$.

proof.text:
In a decomposition $p=p_1+\cdots+p_t$ with all $p_i
e0$, strict positivity and integral weights give $w(p)=\sum_iw(p_i)\ge t$. For $p
e0$ the length set is nonempty (the one-term decomposition) and is a subset of the finite interval $\{1,\ldots,w(p)\}$, hence has an attained largest element. A nonempty sum cannot be zero since its weight is positive. Thus the empty decomposition alone represents zero, $
u(0)=0$, and $
u(p)\le w(p)$ for every $p$. In Lean, define each maximum by Nat.findGreatest with bound $w(p).\mathrm{toNat}$; the singleton or empty decomposition supplies a witness, and the weight inequality proves that this bounded search is the greatest of all lengths.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: maximal lengths from positive integral weights

proof.text:
If $r=0$, the fixed lattice coordinates identify $G$ with the zero group, so $P=\{0\}$, $S_n=\{0\}$, and $F(n)=\lambda(n)$; take $a\prime=a$, $b\prime=b$, $n_0=k_0$. Henceforth suppose $r>0$. Remove zero from a finite monoid generating list. The remaining list is nonempty since its generated subgroup is the nonzero group $G$. Each $w(g_i)\ge1$, so $M\ge1$. For any $p$ write $p=\sum_{i=1}^s a_ig_i$ with $a_i\in\mathbf N$ and put $t=\sum_i a_i$. Then $t\le
u(p)$ and $w(p)=\sum_i a_iw(g_i)\le Mt\le M
u(p)$. This proves $w(p)/M\le
u(p)\le w(p)$, including $p=0$. The formal proof takes a finite word in the nonzero generators using AddSubmonoid.exists_list_of_mem_closure, and regards that word as a decomposition indexed by Fin of its length. This is the same count as the sum of multiplicities above.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: rank zero and generator-length comparison

proof.text: Fix lattice coordinates using the finite integral basis of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. In the generator expression of Step 2, $t\le\nu(p)$, so for $p\in S_n$ each coordinate satisfies $|p_j|\le\sum_i a_i|(g_i)_j|\le Ct<Cn$. Consequently the injective coordinate map sends $S_n$ into $\{-Cn,\ldots,Cn\}^r$, a finite product of $r$ intervals each of cardinality $2Cn+1$. Thus $S_n$ is finite and $|S_n|\le(2Cn+1)^r$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: upper coordinate box

proof.text: View the integral coordinate vectors $g_i$ in $\mathbf Q^r$. Each standard coordinate vector $e_j$ is an integer combination of the $g_i$, because the generated subgroup is all of $G$. Thus these rational vectors span $\mathbf Q^r$. Apply [lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily] with field $\mathbf Q$ to obtain an independent subfamily with the same span. By [lem-weil-dimension-span-independent-family], its size is the dimension of this span; applying that same statement to the standard coordinate basis shows this dimension is $r$. Denote the selected generators by $v_1,\ldots,v_r$. Their rational independence implies integral independence, since an integral relation is in particular a rational relation. Mathlib Submodule.exists_fun_fin_finrank_span_eq packages the independent-subfamily and dimension statements into a family indexed by Fin r. The rational span is all of the coordinate space by subgroup closure induction; LinearIndependent.restrict_scalars' and LinearIndependent.of_comp transfer independence back to the integral generators.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: selection of independent generators

proof.text: For any such independent choice let $W=\max_j w(v_j)\ge1$, $n\ge2$, and $m=\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor$. If $0\le b_j\le m$, then $p=\sum_jb_jv_j$ belongs to $P$ and $\nu(p)\le w(p)=\sum_jb_jw(v_j)\le rmW\le n/4$. Equality of the images of two tuples gives the integral relation $\sum_j(b_j-b\prime_j)v_j=0$, forcing equality of all entries. Thus the tuple map is injective, with $(m+1)^r$ image points. Each image point belongs to $S_n$ and has $n-\nu(p)\ge3n/4\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor\ge1$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: independent-generator lower box using the weight upper bound on length

proof.text:
For $p\in S_n$, $1\le n-
u(p)\le n$ and monotonicity gives $\lambda(n-
u(p))\le\lambda(n)$. Summing and applying Step 3 proves the stated upper convolution bound. On every image point of Step 5, monotonicity gives $\lambda(n-
u(p))\ge\lambda(\lfloor n/2floor)$. All remaining summands are nonnegative, so restricting the sum to these $(m+1)^r$ points proves the stated lower convolution bound for every $n\ge2$. In Lean, use the finite subtype of points with length below n; finsum_eq_sum_of_fintype identifies its finsum with a Finset sum. For the lower bound, sum over the image of the injective box map and compare that image sum with the full sum.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70; agent-supplied lattice refinement: finite nonnegative sum comparison

proof.text: For $n\ge n_0=\max(3,2k_0)$, one has $\lfloor n/2\rfloor\ge k_0$ and $\lfloor n/2\rfloor\ge n/3$. Also $\lfloor n/(4rW)\rfloor+1\ge n/(4rW)$ and $2Cn+1\le(2C+1)n$. Substitute the assumed polynomial bounds at $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and $n$ into Step 6. The result is $\bigl(a\,3^{-d}(4rW)^{-r}\bigr)n^{d+r}\le F(n)\le\bigl(b(2C+1)^r\bigr)n^{d+r}$. Both displayed constants are positive; these give $a\prime,b\prime$ and complete the assertion. The inequalities also cover $d=0$, since every positive number to the zeroth power is one.
